newsitem.title: INDIA: India could buy 3,000 mw power from Pakistan - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India could buy 3,000 mw power from Pakistan - PTI.

text.p: India is considering buying 3,000 megawatts of power from Pakistan, the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted a government minister as saying.

The news agency quoted junior Power Minister S. Venugopalachari as telling reporters on Sunday in the southern city of Bangalore that the two nations' foreign secretaries would discuss the possible purchase in coming talks.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral last week cited the purchase of surplus power from Pakistan as one of the agreements that could be reached in bilateral talks between the longtime foes. He did not say how much power could be bought.
Gujral met his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, on the fringes of a regional summit in the Maldives last week.
The foreign secretaries -- the nations' highest ranking civil servants in the foreign ministries -- are expected to hold talks in late June in Islamabad.
Power from Pakistan would be transmitted from Lahore to the northern Indian state of Punjab, PTI said.
Venugopalachari said the World Bank had urged Pakistan to share surplus power from the Indus River basin with neighbouring countries.
